summary.what_it_does: Derives the groups of connected people that structure the scrolling narrative, keeping only groups anchored by main subjects. It orders those circles by the main subjects’ birth years and supplies their internal relationships for the narration phase.
summary.why_this_design: It recomputes the circles with the same deterministic rules as the client so narration keys continue to match the groups shown in the interface without storing a second version.

summary.what_it_does: Builds the collection’s editorial frame by selecting people whose records directly support the topic, then arranging them into themes and eras with an opening narrative and conclusion. It also identifies absent people who would fill gaps in the dataset and strengthen the eventual story.
summary.why_this_design: It supplies event locations and titles alongside abbreviated biographies so selection can recognize substantive place-based and topic-specific work, while manual choices and explicit hints can override automated relevance judgments.

summary.what_it_does: Collects dated life events for every person selected in the plan, attaches each event to its person, and orders the combined list by year. It leaves later selection and chapter assignment to downstream steps while giving them a chronological record of the available evidence.
summary.why_this_design: It ignores the early chapter ranges because those ranges were inferred from incomplete summaries and could otherwise exclude events before they can be judged for relevance.

summary.what_it_does: Judges each person’s biographical events against the meta-story’s theme and keeps only landmark contributions with a concrete, lasting result. It records a short explanation for every decision, giving later stages both a sparse set of candidate events and the rationale for excluding background and career context.
summary.why_this_design: It treats an unjudged batch as a failure rather than admitting its events, protecting the story from turning a filtering error into false historical significance.

summary.what_it_does: Places every curated event in a planned chapter, assigning events outside the proposed ranges to the nearest chapter. It then resets each retained chapter’s dates to its events and drops chapters with no events, leaving a continuous event-backed timeline for the meta story.
summary.why_this_design: Treating planned ranges as guidance rather than filters prevents curation survivors from disappearing at chapter boundaries while preserving the planned chapter order.

summary.what_it_does: Places each chapter in its wider period by adding only discrete historical events that concretely changed the featured people’s lives, work, or circumstances. It uses the chapter dates and existing person events to keep that context tied to the story rather than to the era in general.
summary.why_this_design: It permits empty chapters and bars repeated or overlapping events so background landmarks do not crowd out the people’s own events or turn the timeline into generic history.

summary.what_it_does: Combines the selected people’s ego networks into a single graph. It preserves direct ties among the main people and adds only acquaintances who connect more than one of them, leaving the story with a compact view of shared social context.
summary.why_this_design: It matches names before merging and retains the richest account of each tie, while keeping both directions of a direct relationship so the interface can describe it from either person’s perspective.

summary.what_it_does: Reviews the derived social graph against the article evidence, adding missed direct ties and correcting or removing weak ones before clustering turns the graph into circles. It preserves the existing graph when review cannot run or when there are too few main people to form a network.
summary.why_this_design: The step adjusts its standard for additions and deletions to the graph's existing density, so it can fill genuine gaps in a sparse graph without making a dense graph less discriminating.

summary.what_it_does: Turns each deterministic social circle’s recorded ties into a short card narrative for the meta story. It preserves the cluster order and keys while giving the network a readable account of the bonds and bridging acquaintances behind each group.
summary.why_this_design: It treats narration as optional because the interface can fall back to the underlying ties, allowing the story to remain usable when this generation or later composition fails.

summary.what_it_does: Groups rated events into geographically compact map stops, then carries forward the strongest clusters with their locations, time span, and ordered events. It orders the selected stops by time so the map follows the story’s chronology rather than its ranking.
summary.why_this_design: Complete-linkage merging prevents a chain of nearby events from turning into one geographically sprawling stop, while rating-based selection keeps the map focused on events the story has judged consequential.

summary.what_it_does: Rates each located event by whether the event and its place together carry the story’s theme. Leaves those ratings as weights for the map’s later clustering, so places tied to defining work or gatherings can shape the route more than incidental venues.
summary.why_this_design: It runs before clustering because the map should group around places that advance the story, while a failed or partial batch leaves events at a neutral weight instead of removing them from the map.

summary.what_it_does: Turns chronological place clusters into concise map-card stories, linking local events to the larger meta-story. It also decides which clusters deserve a stop, so weak or incidental places do not survive into the map.
summary.why_this_design: It combines narration with curation because a place-based interface needs a small sequence of consequential locations rather than a complete list of where events occurred.

summary.what_it_does: Composes the page as a single account after earlier steps have drafted its individual parts. It sets the story’s arc and reading order, rewrites the surrounding prose and component text in one voice, and can remove map stops that no longer serve that account.
summary.why_this_design: It reads the assembled material top-down so it can make choices about emphasis, sequence, and omission that item-by-item drafting could not make.

summary.what_it_does: Writes the completed story document to its stable location, creating the story directory when needed. Returns failure instead of leaving the caller to infer whether the story became available.
summary.why_this_design: It creates the directory before writing so a first run can publish a story without a separate setup step.

summary.what_it_does: Builds the visual identity for the meta story, choosing its dark palette, typography, box treatment, and a theme-derived geometric pattern. It also creates matching separator and closing-rule marks so the long article, timeline, network, and map read as parts of one editorial system.
summary.why_this_design: It limits the background pattern to calm, seamless black-and-white geometry so the page can keep a distinctive theme without competing with long passages of text.

summary.what_it_does: Translates a meta-story detail file when its target-language copy is stale, saves the translated file, and updates the language registry so the story is available with the rest of that language’s material.
summary.why_this_design: It reuses the person translations’ event titles and name forms so story slides and chapters refer to the same people and events in the same words.

summary.what_it_does: Writes the long-form background passages for only the events the story exposes as depth layers, using the reviewed event record, the subject’s article, related articles, and the surrounding story outline. It also replaces each event’s citations with shown, event-specific sources and passes report details to image selection, then carries the source corrections into translated copies.
summary.why_this_design: Limits work to the interface’s deep-event selection so no unreachable report is created, while filtering citations to supplied URLs prevents plausible but unsupported links from appearing beside the passage.

summary.what_it_does: Creates an abstract illustration for each chapter concept, using the portrait style reference to carry the story’s light-drawn visual language into chapter slides. It returns image bytes when generation succeeds and lets the run continue when an individual chapter image fails.
summary.why_this_design: It uses the reference only for rendering style and forbids people, places, and text so the chapter image can suggest an idea without competing with the portraits or asserting facts the story has not established.

summary.what_it_does: Creates an abstract opening-image concept for each chapter from the person’s biography, leaving later illustration work with a visual metaphor rather than a literal scene. It returns only concepts attached to existing chapter IDs, so unusable or mismatched results do not alter the story.
summary.why_this_design: It considers every chapter together so the chapter images use distinct forms and metaphors instead of repeating the same visual language.

summary.what_it_does: Groups the established events into chronological life phases and gives each phase a story-led headline, a broad setting, and the people who matter within it. It also supplies the closing statement that turns the event record into a personal narrative with an ending.
summary.why_this_design: It fails the run rather than return an unchaptered record because the chapters provide the narrative structure that makes the collected events read as a life story.

summary.what_it_does: Adds biographical evidence for German and European figures, including dates, places, occupations, work locations, relationships, and genealogy when available. It omits the source entirely when no matching record was found, leaving later stages with only usable evidence.
summary.why_this_design: Keeps article text out of prompts when its license prohibits derivatives, while retaining the separately licensed metadata that can still support identification and context.

summary.what_it_does: Builds the biographical spine from the main article, using related articles only to clarify context. It selects and orders the subject’s defining life events, assigns dates and relative importance, and leaves later steps a factual outline to enrich with places, images, and sources.
summary.why_this_design: Because significance is relative within one life, this is the only step that can rank events against each other while seeing the full article set; it also keeps event descriptions in their own moment so later legacy claims do not distort the chronology.

summary.what_it_does: Researches one biographical event against the subject’s article and event-specific related articles, enriching the timeline with grounded narrative context, places, participants, supporting sources, visual search leads, and a semantic icon. Leaves an unresolved event in the story when the research call fails rather than dropping it.
summary.why_this_design: It treats the subject’s article as the authority and admits related articles only when they document the event, which keeps added detail tied to the life narrative instead of nearby but irrelevant material.

summary.what_it_does: Resolves each selected place name to map coordinates, trying normalized variants when the first spelling does not match. It reuses prior results and skips unknown labels so repeated locations do not trigger another lookup.
summary.why_this_design: It records a miss only after every candidate has produced a definitive nonmatch, allowing later runs to retry requests disrupted by a transient lookup failure.

summary.what_it_does: Decides which people in a biography have an established target-language form and records only the names that should change. Later translation work uses that shared glossary so the same person appears under one spelling across documents and cross-references.
summary.why_this_design: It favors unchanged names and treats source-language evidence as spelling evidence, while rejecting mismatched subjects, expanded titles, and altered regnal numbering; a failed lookup also leaves names unchanged rather than introducing inconsistent substitutions.

summary.what_it_does: Judges Commons search results against the background report and keeps only images that directly show a named thing in the account. It returns a small set of distinct illustrations after excluding the event image already shown.
summary.why_this_design: It treats search results as untrusted word matches—using filenames as well as captions—and enforces one image per query in code so related but wrong results or duplicate views do not fill the report.

summary.what_it_does: Searches image archives with both broad person queries and event-specific queries, returning one deduplicated pool of image candidates. It marks images found through event searches so later matching can connect them to the event that prompted the search.
summary.why_this_design: It searches event queries first and keeps the first copy of a URL, preserving event provenance when the same image appears in broader results; it limits those targeted searches to the archive best suited to named objects while using the second source to broaden person searches.

summary.what_it_does: Scores the shared image pool, removes weak candidates, and orders the remainder before later matching links images to events. It keeps the score with each image so later stages can inspect the basis for the ranking.
summary.why_this_design: The callers omit event-specific signals because the pool is scored once and reused across events, avoiding a separate ranking pass for each event.

summary.what_it_does: Selects a reference portrait and places only directly relevant Commons images beside life events, using filenames and source metadata to write cautious captions. It leaves unsupported events unillustrated and preserves the selected image’s attribution data for later display.
summary.why_this_design: It treats search results as leads rather than evidence and prevents the portrait or a commemorative stand-in from becoming a misleading substitute for an event.

summary.what_it_does: Builds a shared set of Commons searches from the full event list, reserving person-name searches for portrait selection and directing the rest toward the named objects, works, and institutions that carry the life story. This gives later image selection candidates tied to events rather than to isolated places or occupations.
summary.why_this_design: It excludes commemorations because Commons searches that join a person to a place often surface plaques, graves, and statues made after the life instead of images of what the person encountered or made.

summary.what_it_does: Checks the selected portrait against the person named in the story by examining the image itself. It rejects picks that show a related person, an object, or an unidentifiable group despite metadata that mentions the subject.
summary.why_this_design: It treats a failed check as inconclusive so an unavailable verification call cannot discard an otherwise usable portrait; the check only removes clear mismatches introduced by metadata-based matching.

summary.what_it_does: Reads the target-language article for the person and follows language links for the person’s names and places. Leaves the later translation calls with names already used by that language, reducing guesses based on the translator’s memory.
summary.why_this_design: It treats the lookup as optional so missing coverage or network access does not stop translation, and tries comma-separated place names intact before looking up their leading name so a found full title wins while any regional qualifier remains available to translate.

summary.what_it_does: Builds a sourced map of the subject’s important family, work, social, and political ties from the main article and related Wikipedia pages. It turns those ties into a small set of relationship circles whose summaries explain how each circle shaped the person’s life and work.
summary.why_this_design: It keeps one entry per connected person while separating category and role, so the later story can combine several aspects of a tie without duplicating people or drifting outside the interface’s relationship vocabulary.

summary.what_it_does: Transforms each person’s source portrait into a shared light-drawing treatment while keeping the person’s likeness, pose, expression, and period clothing recognizable. It leaves a portrait asset that makes individual stories read as part of the same visual collection.
summary.why_this_design: It assigns separate roles to the source portrait and master reference so the common style does not replace the historical subject’s identity, and it rejects inherited frames that would turn archival portrait conventions into part of the collection’s visual language.

summary.what_it_does: Resolves unlinked publication events to a place where the work can be read, checking Wikidata first and Wikipedia when needed. Adds a link only after the work’s title and the named person’s authorship agree, so publication slides point to the intended work rather than a title match.
summary.why_this_design: It treats missing links and failed lookups as normal, while caching results, so an unavailable service or an uncertain match does not interrupt generation or turn repeated searches into repeated network calls.

summary.what_it_does: Updates the landing-page record for a person with the story’s current name, summary, dates, roles, and portrait reference. It preserves the original appearance date, removes a portrait field when the story explicitly has none, then saves the register in name order.
summary.why_this_design: The update keeps the first-seen timestamp because later story runs revise the person’s details rather than create a new registry entry.

summary.what_it_does: Reviews the generated life events and relationship network against the available Wikipedia material, then proposes corrections and editorial changes across both. It treats the two views of a person as one story, checking that people, claims, and emphasis agree rather than reviewing each file in isolation.
summary.why_this_design: Reviewing the event timeline and network together exposes missing connections and repeated or conflicting descriptions that separate critic passes would miss.

summary.what_it_does: Reviews a biography page’s colors, pattern, and fonts against the subject’s life, era, and roles. It returns an assessment and recommends changes only when the existing style has a clear problem or missed opportunity.
summary.why_this_design: The review treats the generated style as presumptively sound, which limits cosmetic churn while still checking readability, cultural fit, and the pattern’s hard rendering constraints.

summary.what_it_does: Derives the story’s dark-mode visual identity from the subject’s era, field, and character. It returns a color palette, paired type choices, and abstract geometric SVG elements that carry those cues into the interface.
summary.why_this_design: It restricts the repeating pattern to black and white and uses stroke weight rather than opacity so the pattern stays legible and consistent behind the story’s content.

summary.what_it_does: Translates the extracted prose for a person record while preserving its document structure and annotation links. It supplies the name glossary and target-language reference evidence so localized names stay consistent with the rest of the record before the translated fields are merged back into the English document.
summary.why_this_design: It sends only text that may change and overlays the result onto the original record, which protects dates, coordinates, URLs, IDs, and other fixed data from translation errors.

summary.what_it_does: Fetches a subject’s main Wikipedia article, related articles, and Commons image metadata, then stores the material for later phases. It lets later runs reuse the cached record instead of repeating external requests.
summary.why_this_design: When a URL replaces the subject for retrieval, it preserves the supplied subject-derived identifier so downstream records keep a stable identity.

summary.what_it_does: Ranks links from a person’s Wikipedia article and keeps the ones most likely to add biographical evidence: people in the subject’s life, specific events, and personal works. It leaves later retrieval focused on relationships and turning points rather than broad background.
summary.why_this_design: It excludes places, institutions, fields, and other general context so the limited follow-up material supports a life narrative instead of crowding it with reference material.

summary.what_it_does: Writes the assembled life-events document to the person’s directory and returns its path. This makes the generated account a durable dataset that later stages read instead of the in-memory payload.
summary.why_this_design: Creates the person-specific directory before writing so a new person can complete the pipeline without relying on prior filesystem setup.
